contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #274: Parity is not in QAC<sup>0</sup>.
Dimension- and rank-uniform localization on N finite-dimensional tensor sites, for arbitrary local-projection counts and circuits with d disjoint product-reflection layers.

definitions.count: sum_i(I-P_i), with arbitrary local orthogonal projections P_i; uncounted sites have P_i=I
definitions.depth: number of disjoint product-reflection layers; arbitrary tensor-product local unitaries are free
definitions.uniform: the site threshold depends only on the fixed depth and exponents, never on local dimensions, ranks, or circuit entries

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 274 (Parity is not in QAC<sup>0</sup>.; papers: Product-projection localization and the QAC0 parity lower bound; Regular trajectories, pruning and quantum parity; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/274.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.
The staged papers prove different qubit/rank-one dependency chains; neither asserts the dimension- and rank-uniform extension.
First manuscript, lem:polynomial: an integer zero filter has degree and weighted coefficient logarithm below N^u for u>(a+b)/2.
First manuscript, lem:base: rank-one product factors give a depth-zero squared transition bound 2^(-r).
First manuscript, lem:propagation: previous-depth localization extends from a zero pattern to all low-count patterns.
First manuscript, lem:small-support: ordered reflection expansion costs at most 9^k and reduces a k-site projection by one depth.
First manuscript, lem:backward: under the previous-depth hypothesis, B_d(t,b) implies B_d(s,t) whenever s<t<b<2t-s.
First manuscript, thm:localization: uniform qubit product-projection localization at every fixed depth and exponent pair.
First manuscript, thm:parity: complementary Hadamard matrix entries and character orthogonality convert localization to a measured-output parity lower bound.
Second manuscript, lem:degree-shift: operator degree bounds excitation shifts.
Second manuscript, lem:zero-filter and lem:tail-filter: integer zero approximation and a globally nonnegative tail polynomial with global growth control.
Second manuscript, prop:propagation: low-degree perturbations propagate along an assumed regular trajectory, using a qubit Pauli coefficient bound.
Second manuscript, lem:tail-transport: two already regular trajectories linked by an endpoint projection transfer excitation tails.
Second manuscript, prop:projection-insertion: backward suffix induction preserves regularity after an endpoint product projection.
Second manuscript, cor:product-tail and cor:overlap-tail: for a regular product-input trajectory the output tail is multiplied by the projection probability, not its square root.
Second manuscript, lem:retained-layer: mean counts, binary low-weight atom counting, and recentering make gates with probability at least m^(-6) regular.
Second manuscript, prop:pruning: prefix induction yields a regular pruned circuit within vector distance 2t m^(-2) on the specified product input.
Second manuscript, thm:parity: reference copies, pruning, and the product-input tail contradict fixed measured-output parity advantage.
For arbitrary idempotents P,Q in a unital ring, P-PQ(2-P)QP=(P-PQP)^2; for orthogonal projections the right side is a positive square.
For arbitrary local orthogonal projections and r>=0, the squared product-projection transition from the zero count is at most 2^(-r), including entangled zero-sector inputs.

Under the full dimension-uniform previous-depth hypothesis, binary subspace patterns, ordered reflection expansion, polynomial coefficient control, and inverse substitution give the backward implication at dimension-free thresholds.

For every fixed d and 0<=s<t there exists N0(d,s,t) such that arbitrary finite local dimensions, arbitrary-rank product-reflection circuits at depth d, and arbitrary local-projection counts M,D satisfy ||[M>=N^t]U[D=0]U*[M=0]||<=exp(-N^s) for N>=N0.

For arbitrary higher-rank local projections, a normalized product projection applied to every vector in a product zero-count subspace produces independent binary mismatch outcomes on the counted sites.
The staged papers prove different qubit/rank-one dependency chains; neither asserts the dimension- and rank-uniform extension.

claims.natural_statement: For arbitrary finite complex matrices representing orthogonal projections P,Q, B=PQ(2I-P)QP and P-B are positive semidefinite with explicit Gram identities; positive tensor-order composition and the nonnegative-scalar compressed-tail implication hold for arbitrary finite matrix sizes.
claims.formal_statement:
import Mathlib

open scoped Kronecker ComplexOrder

namespace DimensionUniform

theorem projection_defect {R : Type*} [Ring R] (P Q : R)
    (hP : P * P = P) (hQ : Q * Q = Q) :
    P - P * Q * (2 - P) * Q * P =
      (P - P * Q * P) * (P - P * Q * P) := by
  have hPP (X : R) : P * (P * X) = P * X := by
    rw [← mul_assoc, hP]
  have hQQ (X : R) : Q * (Q * X) = Q * X := by
    rw [← mul_assoc, hQ]
  noncomm_ring [hP, hQ, hPP, hQQ]

section Matrices

variable {n m : Type*} [Fintype n] [Fintype m] [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq m]

theorem projection_defect_gram (P Q : Matrix n n ℂ)
    (hP : P * P = P) (hQ : Q * Q = Q)
    (hPs : Pᴴ = P) (hQs : Qᴴ = Q) :
    P - P * Q * (2 - P) * Q * P =
      (P - P * Q * P)ᴴ * (P - P * Q * P) := by
  have hs : (P - P * Q * P)ᴴ = P - P * Q * P := by
    simp only [Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hPs, hQs, mul_assoc]
  rw [hs]
  exact projection_defect P Q hP hQ

theorem weighted_projection_contraction (P Q : Matrix n n ℂ)
    (hP : P * P = P) (hQ : Q * Q = Q)
    (hPs : Pᴴ = P) (hQs : Qᴴ = Q) :
    (P - P * Q * (2 - P) * Q * P).PosSemidef := by
  rw [projection_defect_gram P Q hP hQ hPs hQs]
  exact Matrix.posSemidef_conjTranspose_mul_self _

theorem weighted_projection_gram (P Q : Matrix n n ℂ)
    (hP : P * P = P) (hPs : Pᴴ = P) (hQs : Qᴴ = Q) :
    P * Q * (2 - P) * Q * P =
      (Q * P)ᴴ * (Q * P) +
        ((1 - P) * Q * P)ᴴ * ((1 - P) * Q * P) := by
  have hPP (X : Matrix n n ℂ) : P * (P * X) = P * X := by
    rw [← mul_assoc, hP]
  simp only [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, Matrix.conjTranspose_sub,
    Matrix.conjTranspose_one, hPs, hQs]
  noncomm_ring [hP, hPP]

theorem weighted_projection_positive (P Q : Matrix n n ℂ)
    (hP : P * P = P) (hPs : Pᴴ = P) (hQs : Qᴴ = Q) :
    (P * Q * (2 - P) * Q * P).PosSemidef := by
  rw [weighted_projection_gram P Q hP hPs hQs]
  exact (Matrix.posSemidef_conjTranspose_mul_self _).add
    (Matrix.posSemidef_conjTranspose_mul_self _)

theorem projection_positive (P : Matrix n n ℂ)
    (hP : P * P = P) (hPs : Pᴴ = P) : P.PosSemidef := by
  simpa only [hPs, hP] using Matrix.posSemidef_conjTranspose_mul_self P

theorem tensor_order_step (A B : Matrix n n ℂ) (C D : Matrix m m ℂ)
    (hA : A.PosSemidef) (hD : D.PosSemidef)
    (hBA : (B - A).PosSemidef) (hDC : (D - C).PosSemidef) :
    (B ⊗ₖ D - A ⊗ₖ C).PosSemidef := by
  have hid : B ⊗ₖ D - A ⊗ₖ C =
      (B - A) ⊗ₖ D + A ⊗ₖ (D - C) := by
    ext i j
    simp only [Matrix.sub_apply, Matrix.add_apply, Matrix.kronecker_apply]
    ring
  rw [hid]
  exact (hBA.kronecker hD).add (hA.kronecker hDC)

theorem compressed_tail (K P W H : Matrix n n ℂ) (c : ℝ)
    (hc : 0 ≤ c)
    (hW : (P - Kᴴ * W * K).PosSemidef)
    (hH : (c • W - H).PosSemidef) :
    (c • P - Kᴴ * H * K).PosSemidef := by
  have hid : c • P - Kᴴ * H * K =
      c • (P - Kᴴ * W * K) + Kᴴ * (c • W - H) * K := by
    simp only [smul_sub, mul_sub, sub_mul, mul_smul_comm, smul_mul_assoc]
    abel
  rw [hid]
  exact (hW.smul hc).add (hH.conjTranspose_mul_mul_same K)

end Matrices

end DimensionUniform

claims.natural_statement: Assuming all dimension-uniform depth-(d-1) localization pairs, binary subspace patterns give ||[M>=N^beta]B[M<N^alpha]||<=exp(-N^sigma) for beta>max(alpha,sigma), with a threshold depending only on depth and the exponents.

Assuming all dimension-uniform depth-(d-1) localization pairs, depth-d conjugation of product projections on at most N^u sites has transition at most exp(-N^w) to count N^t for t>max(u,w); the reflection expansion costs at most 9^k.

For fixed 0<a<b and u>(a+b)/2, the explicit root-Chebyshev polynomial has p(0)=1, degree and log weighted coefficient norm at most N^u, and integer error at most exp(-N^a) through ceil(N^b), with no b<=1 restriction.

Assuming all dimension-uniform depth-(d-1) pairs and the universal same-depth pair B_d(t,b), one-sided polynomial substitution after squaring and exact inverse count exchange prove B_d(s,t) whenever 0<=s<t<b<2t-s.

For every 0<=s<t<=1 the recurrence with eta=(t-s)^2/100 reaches a tail exponent greater than one within ceil(2/(t-s)) steps, keeping t_i<t_(i+1)<2t_i-s_i; hence the conditional backward implication yields all depth-d pairs from the previous-depth theorem.

Under the full dimension-uniform previous-depth hypothesis, binary subspace patterns, ordered reflection expansion, coefficient-controlled polynomials, inverse count exchange, and the finite scale induction prove every depth-d localization pair with dimension-free thresholds.

routes.retired_because: An entangled vector in higher-rank counted zero subspaces can have correlated binary mismatch outcomes. Rank-one scalar independence cannot be imported; the active route is an operator-valued contraction.
